sentences.text: Shri Dharmendra Rishishwar- learned counsel for the appe  Shri A.K.Nirankari- learned Public Prosecutor for the re Per Justice Deepak Kumar Agarwal:-

Heard on IA No. 4179 of 2023, second application under Section 389(1) of CrPC filed on behalf of appellant Shakil Khan for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail.
First application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 02-12-2022.

Appellant has been sentenced to undergo ten years RI with fine of Rs.2,000/- for offence under Section 392 of IPC, ten years RI with fine of Rs. 1,000/- for offence under Section 394 read with Section 397 of IPC, ten years RI with fine of Rs.1,000/-
for offence under Section 460 of IPC, one year RI with fine of Rs. 1,000/- for offence under Section 25(1-b)(A) of the Arms Act and three years RI with fine of Rs.1,000/-
for offence under Section 11/13 of MPDVPK Act with default stipulations vide judgment judgment dated 10/02/2021 passed by Special Judge (MPDVPK Act)
Gohad, District Bhind in Special Sessions Trial No.03 of 2017.
All the sentences have been directed to run concurrently.
Prosecution story found to be proved against the appellant and co-convicted accused is that on 24/12/2016 complainant Ramkumar Gupta came at Gwalior leaving behind his mother and father at home.
On 25/12/2016, one Girraj Gupta telephoned him and told that his mother and father are in an injured condition and goods of his house are scattered.

When he came there, he found that gold and silver ornaments weighing 45 Tola as well as cash which was kept in Office, shop and in almiraha of his mother more than Rs.2,00,000/- were missing.
Thereafter, FIR was lodged against the unknown persons bearing Crime No.376/2016 at Police Station Gohad, District Bhind (M.P.) for offences under Sections 394, 459, 412, 397, 411, 414 of IPC and Sections 25/27 of Arms Act and Sections 11/13 of MPDVPK Act.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant has been falsely implicated.
The appellant is in custody since 01-05-2017.

He has already served more Shakil Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199983452/
1 than five years ten months jail sentence.

sentences.text: There are fair chances of success of this appeal and the appeal may take long time for its conclusion.

It is further contended that jail sentence of co-convicted accused Najreen Khan has already been suspended by this Court vide order dated 02/09/2022 passed in Criminal Appeal No.1747 of 2021 and jail sentence of co-convicted accused Smt. Preeti Baghel has already been suspended by this Court vide order dated 16-09-2022 passed in Criminal Appeal No.1682 of 2021.
Under these circumstances, execution of sentence be suspended and the appellant be released on bail.
Per contra, the learned Public Prosecutor for the respondent State opposes the application and prayed for its rejection.

Considering the arguments advanced by counsel for the parties as well as the fact that execution of jail sentence of co-convicted accused Najreen Khan and Smt. Preeti Baghel has already been suspended by this Court coupled with the fact that the appellant has already served more than five years ten months jail sentence out of jail sentence awarded by the trial Court and there is no possibility of early hearing of the appeal in near future, therefore, it is directed that the jail sentence of appellant shall remain suspended and he be released on bail, subject to depositing the amount of fine (if not already deposited) and on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/-(Rupees fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the Registry of this Court on 7th August, 2023 and on such other subsequent dates as may be fixed by the Office in this regard.
IA stands allowed and disposed of.
CC as per rules.
